title: CRLR/878/2024 of PRASHANT BHATT Vs SHWETA SHARMA

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.878 of 2024
Prashant Bhatt .......Revisionist

Present:-
Mr. Mayank Badoni and Mr. Naveen Singh Bisht,
Advocates for the revisionist.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to an order
dated 09.10.2024, passed in Criminal Case No. 21 of 2021,
Smt. Shweta Sharma Vs. Sri Prashant Bhatt, by the court of
Principal Judge, Family Court, Dehradun ("the case"). By it,
the revisionist has been directed to pay Rs.25,000/- per
month as interim maintenance to the respondent.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. The case is based on an application filed under
Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the
Code") by the respondent. According to it, the respondent
and the revisionist were married on 28.04.2015. The
revisionist was staying in Japan. He took the respondent to
join his company in Japan, where the revisionist is working
as Project Manager in a company. He would not maintain
the respondent in Japan. He would neglect her. He would

2
ignore her, did maar-peet and took fights on small issues.
The respondent had to do some jobs to run her home, but
the fights, daily quarrels and abuses increased.
4. It has been the case of the respondent that the
revisionist was in habit of drinking. His hands would shiver
due to excessive drinking. He would not maintain himself.
Finally, the respondent left the company of the revisionist
and returned to India on 24.10.2019. She is not able to
maintain herself. Whereas, the revisionist is an employed
and gets 7 Lakh Yen, per month (approximately Rs.5 Lakh
per month).
5. The revisionist denied all the allegations.
According to the revisionist, it is the respondent who created
pressure on him to pay money to her parents. It is a case of
the revisionist that the respondent is trying to implicate the
family of the revisionist in a false and trying to extort a sum
of Rs.30 Lakh. With regard to the respondent, the revisionist
writes that she is highly educated and a qualified woman
and employed before marriage. She was also employed
during her stay in Japan.
6. In the case, an application for interim
maintenance was filed, which has been allowed by the
impugned order.

3
7. Learned counsel appearing for the revisionist
would submit that the impugned order is bad in the eye of
law; material facts have not been considered. He would
submit that, in fact, the revisionist had filed an application
directing the respondent to file certain details, but that
application has not been decided by the court below. In fact,
it is argued that the revisionist did file second application
with the same relief, which is still pending.
8. Learned counsel would submit that on
24.10.2019, when the respondent returned to India, she
had returned with a returned ticket, but she did not return
Japan to join the company of the revisionist. She is staying
separate without any reasonable cause. She has concealed
as to what are her bank accounts? What is her source of
income? What is she doing in Germany? It has also been
argued by the learned counsel for the revisionist that, in
fact, the respondent had concealed that she is in Germany.
Reference has been made to certain documents, which
shows that the respondent is doing her post graduation in
Management.
9. It is a revision. The scope is quite restricted to the
extent of examining the legality, correctness and propriety of
the impugned judgment and order.

4
10. The impugned order is an order for interim
maintenance. The findings are definitely tentative. The
record reveals that, in fact, the revisionist had filed an
application seeking certain details from the respondent with
regard to her immigration, her Visa, her admission matters,
bank details etc. Those applications are still pending. It is
admitted that the revisionist has filed a suit for divorce on
the ground of cruelty against the respondent.
11. Impugned order records that the respondent is
doing post graduation in Management in Germany.
Admittedly, she was working in Japan for which the
respondent has given grounds as to what made her to work
in Japan. The Court need not advert to those facts. Insofar
as, staying separate is concerned, there are divergent
assertions on this point. According to the revisionist, the
respondent is staying separate without any cause. She had
assured to return back to Japan, while leaving Japan, but
she did not return, though she had a returned ticket.
Whereas, according to the respondent, due to harassment,
neglect and torture meted out to her at the hands of the
revisionist, she had to return to India and stayed separate.
She is dependent on her father now for all her expenses.
12. It is also argued that, in fact, the revisionist has
concealed her financial sources. The impugned order itself
records in para 3, page 3 that as per the revisionist, the

5
respondent is studying in Germany and her father finances
her expenses.
13. Even otherwise, if a party conceals any fact or
given any information to the court which is found false, the
court within its jurisdiction may take action for such false
information. As stated, insofar as, the reasons for staying
separate is concerned, the finding recorded in the impugned
order is tentative which would be finally recorded once the
parties are permitted to adduce evidence in the case.
14. In her affidavit of assets and liabilities, the
revisionist has not stated that the respondent in any
manner is employed. The revisionist has stated that the
respondent is well qualified and able bodied and capable of
doing some job as she was working while in Japan. She was
working before her marriage and presently she cannot
remain without work. It is a kind of assumption. On the
other hand, the respondent in her affidavit of assets and
liabilities has categorically stated that she is not earning.
15. Having considered, this Court is of the view that
there is no reason to interfere with the impugned order.
Accordingly, the revision deserves to be dismissed at the
stage of admission itself.

6
16. The revision is dismissed in limine.
(Ravindra Maithani, J)
 12.12.2024
Jitendra
